lead.title: France's HAS rejects early reimbursement for Resilience's Edra Pro psychiatric remote monitoring for a second time
lead.deck: The CNEDiMTS has issued a new unfavourable opinion on early reimbursement (PECAN) for Edra Pro, Resilience's app that collects and analyses patient-reported outcomes and alerts the care team when a patient deteriorates, for adults treated for moderate-to-severe major depressive episodes or bipolar disorder; the new retrospective single-arm observational study and satisfaction survey submitted show some favourable signals, but "no signal was detected on depressive symptoms", the primary endpoint of the pivotal study whose final results are due in May 2027. It is the second refusal after March 2026, and it lands weeks after the €48M raise led by PSG Equity to extend the platform to other specialties and abroad: psychiatry, new ground for this oncology remote-monitoring specialist, will need comparative data before it is reimbursed in France.

milestone.title: At Isala, a digital triage questionnaire before each nephrology follow-up visit shows half of appointments are unnecessary
milestone.summary: In the WACHT-NIET research project, run by the Zwolle hospital with regional GPs, the University of Twente and patients, chronic kidney disease patients receive a short digital questionnaire before their follow-up visit: do they want to see their specialist, and to discuss what? First results published on November 25: in 52% of cases both patient and clinician judged the consultation unnecessary, and total consultation time per patient fell by about 35%; the project is funded by a €499,000 ZonMw grant.
milestone.why: Default follow-up visits for chronic disease are one of the largest pools of hospital capacity: a tool as simple as a pre-visit questionnaire frees up a third of it. For remote follow-up and triage vendors, it is a quantified argument and a model that can be transposed to other chronic specialties.

brefsEurope.title: France's HAS and CNIL publish their final guide on AI in care settings for hospitals and clinicians
brefsEurope.summary: Published on November 27 after a public consultation, the joint guide covers the full lifecycle of an AI system in 11 sheets (governance, procurement and contracting, training, patient information and rights, human oversight, traceability, vigilance, end of life) and will serve as the reference for the AI criteria in hospital certification. For vendors, it sets out what hospitals will now require in their contracts.

brefsEurope.title: France's Court of Audit finds hospital health data warehouses were rolled out without a national strategy
brefsEurope.summary: The report published on November 26 counts 54 hospital warehouses (out of 156 health data warehouses according to the CNIL), funded with €75M from France 2030 across 16 winning projects; it asks the State to clarify its strategy by 2027, calls for mixed funding (self-financing, services, fees under the EHDS) and raises the question of requiring SecNumCloud on top of HDS certification.

brefsEurope.title: France's ANSM records eight medication errors linked to conversational AI advice and warns patients and clinicians
brefsEurope.summary: According to the November 25 statement, eight cases were reported between 2024 and 2026 in patients aged 17 to 89, one of them hospitalised, mostly overdoses (two involving paracetamol) and mix-ups when AI was used to translate reports or prescriptions; the agency, which believes the figure is underestimated, asks for any adverse effect to be reported with a mention of AI use.

brefsEurope.title: CNEDiMTS issues unfavourable opinion on early reimbursement for Ekiyou, an insulin dosing app
brefsEurope.summary: The device targeted people with diabetes on basal-bolus regimens using pens; the commission set aside the qualitative studies on methodological grounds, and the single-arm EKIYOU-Study 1 (16 patients, unpublished) shows no significant difference in time spent between 70 and 180 mg/dl at eight weeks. The week's second PECAN refusal, after Edra Pro.

brefsEurope.title: Germany extends the surcharge for authenticating unknown patients in video consultations until end-2028
brefsEurope.summary: The Extended Evaluation Committee renewed, over the health insurers' objections, EBM code 01444 (10 points, billable once per quarter) that practices receive for manually entering the insurance data of a patient seen by video; it was due to expire at the end of 2026. A review is scheduled by September 30, 2028, depending on whether a nationwide technical identification solution is available.

brefsEurope.title: Five new winners in France 2030's call for digital health experimentation hubs
brefsEurope.summary: Around €1.19M in support for €2.65M of investment: Basolight (AI-assisted imaging, Nice University Hospital), OpMA Prevent (remote follow-up of chronic respiratory failure, HopeCare and Paris Saint-Joseph hospital), PREDIA DT2 (UX Care, Genopole), OnCoChoisit (AI that makes oncology reports understandable, Centre Léon-Bérard) and DÉCLIC (IPSO Santé). The call, run by Banque des Territoires, has €63M until 2027 for a network of 37 hubs.

brefsEurope.title: Digital obesity clinic ViaSlim walks away from its Swiss Dragons' Den deal and plans a raise in early 2027
brefsEurope.summary: Founded in 2024 by physicians Gezim Dervishi and Norbert Niebuhr, the startup (telemedicine, coaching, treatments including GLP-1s, practices in Zurich, Bern and Basel) had accepted CHF 400,000 for 9% on air; it dropped the deal after growing: more than 2,500 active patients, cash-flow positive since Q1 2026, CHF 2.5M revenue targeted this year, and no institutional investor to date.

brefsEurope.title: Preventive medicine clinic AYUN raises more than CHF 900,000 from 93 crowd investors
brefsEurope.summary: The campaign closed on November 27 on Conda.ch to fund the expansion of its Zurich clinic, its technology platform and new locations; AYUN reports around 1,500 customers, CHF 2.7M in revenue since its 2024 launch, its first months of positive EBITDA and its first corporate clients.

word.full: Prise En Charge Anticipée Numérique (early digital reimbursement)
word.definition: A one-year provisional reimbursement by French national health insurance, granted to a digital therapy or remote-monitoring service presumed to be innovative, while it finishes proving its benefit.

parts.label: CNEDiMTS opinion
parts.role: the clinical filter: the HAS judges whether innovation is presumed and whether early data are credible

parts.label: ANS compliance
parts.role: the technical filter: interoperability and security checked by the French digital health agency

parts.label: One-year coverage
parts.role: the financial bridge: exceptional reimbursement ahead of standard listing

how.t: The device operator files on the Convergence (ANS) and Sésame (HAS) platforms; the ANS checks eligibility and compliance with security and interoperability rules.
The CNEDiMTS and the ANS give their opinions, then ministers decide; if approved, the device is reimbursed for one year.
The operator must apply for permanent listing within six months (LPP, for a digital therapy) or nine months (LATM, for remote monitoring), backed by clinical evidence.

word.why: For a French digital health startup, PECAN is often the first reimbursed revenue and the signal investors wait for; but the evidence bar is high: Resilience and Diappymed have just been turned down, and Tilak only secured it after a refusal of standard reimbursement. For a VC, the key question becomes the timeline of comparative trials, not just commercial traction.

startups.name: Tilak Healthcare
startups.use: Odysight, smartphone remote monitoring of chronic maculopathies, reimbursed via PECAN after a favourable HAS opinion in 2025, eight months after an HAS refusal of standard coverage; more than 30,000 patients

startups.name: Poppins (BMotion Technologies)
startups.use: Game-based digital therapy for dyslexia; favourable CNEDiMTS opinion on early reimbursement in June 2026, after a €5M round led by Racine² in 2025

startups.name: Resilience
startups.use: Remote monitoring based on patient-reported outcomes; two PECAN applications for Edra Pro in psychiatry rejected (March and November 2026), pivotal study due in May 2027
